newsitem.title: USA: Pa. local govts face tax, court funding issues - S&P.
newsitem.headline: Pa. local govts face tax, court funding issues - S&P.

text.p: Three continuing tax and spending issues will be key factors affecting Pennsylvania local government credits, Standard & Poor's Corp said Monday.

The rating agency, in an analysis appearing in CreditWeek Municipal, said issues surrounding unitary court funding, the constitutionality of personal property taxes, and the implementation of tax reform are nearing resolution.

On the property tax issue, the state Supreme Court is currently deciding whether the personal property tax is unconstitutional, S&P said. The tax is levied on an individual's interest in out-of-state corporations.
The U.S. Supreme Court recently struck down a similar law in North Carolina.
The state Supreme Court will also decide if previous tax payments must be rebated retroactively if the tax is ruled unconstitutional.
S&P said a county's response to the potential loss of revenue or financial flexibility would be determined on a case-by-case basis.
On other fronts, Pennsylvania is facing a court-imposed timetable to implement a plan to convert to a state-funded court system.
But local governments do not expect a windfall by shifting the funding burden, since the state has said it would reduce other aid proportionately as it assumes the obligation, S&P said.

A third key issue is a tax reform bill pending in the state Senate which would give local governments optional taxing power to cut their reliance on property taxes. The plan would allow local govenrments to impose a personal income tax or an earned income and sales tax as a substitute.

S&P said the plan would be revenue neutral, the agency warned that more budgetary uncertainty could result "as relatively stable propety tax revenues are replaced with potentially less predictable and less stable revenues.
